title: This Ladybug Guards the Parasite That Ate Its Insides

scenes.text: This ladybug is alive. It's guarding its own parasite.
A wasp laid one egg inside it. The larva fed on the ladybug's insides for about 20 days.
Then it chewed its way out and spun a cocoon under the ladybug's legs. The ladybug didn't die.
It stays on top, half paralysed, twitching, for about a week. The twitching scares off hunters.
In the lab, lacewings ate 85 to 100 percent of unguarded cocoons. With a twitching ladybug on top: about 35 percent.
And about a quarter of the ladybugs recover and walk away. Alive, and guarding its own parasite.

description:
The parasitic wasp Dinocampus coccinellae lays an egg in a ladybug; the larva feeds inside for about 20 days, exits and spins its cocoon under the still-living, twitching ladybug.
In a 2011 Biology Letters study (University of Montreal), lacewings ate only about 35 percent of cocoons guarded by a living ladybug, against 85 to 100 percent of cocoons left alone or on a dead one. About 25 percent of the ladybugs recovered afterwards.
Would you rather be the ladybug or the wasp?
subject: ladybug beetle
first_comment: About a quarter of the ladybugs walk away afterwards. Which parasite story should we tell next?
